text.content:
This world has the whole d20 Modern SRD in it: 1,675 documents across sixteen compendia, and 1,685 pages of the rules themselves. Everything below is about the parts a rulebook cannot tell you, because they are about this system rather than about the game.

If you want to play in five minutes

Open the Ready-Made Characters compendium and drag one into the world. There are six, one per basic class, built at first level by the book: maximum hit points, skill points spent to the last one, a starting occupation, a talent, three feats, and the gear to use them. Each carries a note saying why it is put together the way it is.

If you want to make your own

Create an Actor of type hero. The sheet opens on a character creator that walks the SRD's own order: @UUID[Compendium.modern20.rules.JournalEntry.16slDxAW5vS4A9Dt.JournalEntryPage.DL7eGoVYJXLEBKqE]{Ability Scores}, then @UUID[Compendium.modern20.rules.JournalEntry.ygo3sPzJhXS28OXD.JournalEntryPage.6OzOJrAKsG3KzOrC]{Basic Classes}, then @UUID[Compendium.modern20.rules.JournalEntry.J95B9XhYH6v4Joca.JournalEntryPage.WmRPJoGFMoacdRu8]{Occupations}, then @UUID[Compendium.modern20.rules.JournalEntry.Uuaoqg08HvQpYRGt.JournalEntryPage.tnsUcIFoUlGFrR5j]{Skill Basics} and @UUID[Compendium.modern20.rules.JournalEntry.d6dDbFeCTSrHL6vJ.JournalEntryPage.XZV92v0hw7sIw6wt]{Feats}. Nothing is written to the sheet until the step is finished, and every step links to the rules it is applying.

What is a compendium and what is a rule

Every document in every compendium knows the page of the SRD it came from, and says so on its own sheet. The reverse is also true: a rules page lists what it is the rules for, so the page about handguns offers the twenty-three handguns.

Click anything on a sheet that is a number you would roll. An ability, a save, a skill, an attack. The card that comes back says what was rolled, against what, and whether it beat it.

The rules roll themselves

The SRD says what to roll constantly — "a DC 15 Climb check", "a Fortitude save (DC 14)" — and in this world those sentences are the roll. 3,103 of them, on the rules pages and in the items' and creatures' own text, render with a die in front of them; clicking one rolls it for the character you are playing or the token you have selected. Where the SRD printed a DC, the card says whether the roll beat it.

This works in your own notes too: type @Check[skill:climb|dc:15] into any journal page or chat message.

Action points and what happens when you run out of hit points

@UUID[Compendium.modern20.rules.JournalEntry.M6kVCrrZywdkvkEz.JournalEntryPage.aWSa9p2Q7NHK5WqR]{Action Points} are spent to improve a roll you have already made, and the sheet's own box is the place to do it. @UUID[Compendium.modern20.rules.JournalEntry.jKIIXj3FVTQ6RmtB.JournalEntryPage.DYtd2iDnRXllMrpj]{Injury and Death} explains what a character at 0 or fewer hit points is doing; @UUID[Compendium.modern20.rules.JournalEntry.jKIIXj3FVTQ6RmtB.JournalEntryPage.4ufmb54q49RyUIIr]{Massive Damage} is the rule that ends a fight suddenly, and this system applies it automatically unless a setting says otherwise.

Combat

@UUID[Compendium.modern20.rules.JournalEntry.BW08qOlRSlaENtxF.JournalEntryPage.Mg231VpouUwQOIgn]{Combat} and @UUID[Compendium.modern20.rules.JournalEntry.BW08qOlRSlaENtxF.JournalEntryPage.xVeceLLGwBCsmvvL]{Actions in Combat} are the chapters; the sheet tracks what a turn has left in it — an attack action, a move action, a five-foot step — and says so before you spend it twice.

The compendium browser

The compendium sidebar has a Browse button that opens every pack at once, and it filters the way the SRD prices things:

  • by book — d20 Modern, Urban Arcana, d20 Future, the Menace Manual
  • by @UUID[Compendium.modern20.rules.JournalEntry.mHK8Op4Y0OGVi9lU.JournalEntryPage.v7BRwW32qvUoXa3Q]{Wealth}: "what can this character actually afford", which is the question a purchase DC answers
  • by restriction rating — licensed, restricted, military, illegal
  • by progress level, for the d20 Future equipment

Anything in it can be dragged straight onto a sheet or the canvas.

Items on the hotbar

Drag an item from a sheet to the hotbar and it becomes a macro that uses it. The macro finds the item by name on whoever is selected, so one bar works for the whole table, and it survives the item being sold and bought again — which on a @UUID[Compendium.modern20.rules.JournalEntry.mHK8Op4Y0OGVi9lU.JournalEntryPage.v7BRwW32qvUoXa3Q]{Wealth} economy happens constantly.

Equipment

@UUID[Compendium.modern20.rules.JournalEntry.KEk4tUapzxsIoENq.JournalEntryPage.pL1Zl0zJcurgbtLV]{On-Hand Objects} opens the equipment chapter. Purchase DCs, the black market, and what carrying it all does to your speed are applied by the sheet.

Creatures and vehicles

399 actors: every creature in all three books, every vehicle, and the objects the rules let you shoot. Each arrives with the token its stat block implies — the size it occupies in squares, the vision its senses line states, its hit points on a bar — so a Gargantuan wyrm is four squares of wyrm the moment it lands.

Random tables

26 of them, rollable: mutations, cybernetic side effects, where a grenade actually lands, what a celestial is immune to. Each cites the page it was printed on.

FX

@UUID[Compendium.modern20.rules.JournalEntry.hXGxrY1r1Ec6LQTW.JournalEntryPage.KD7TtIMkLsOPA3pD]{FX Basics} covers spells, psionics and the magic items. 174 spells, 87 powers and 147 FX items are in the compendia, with save DCs and casting handled by the sheet.

When something looks wrong

Settings → System Settings → System self-test runs 110 checks inside this world: that every compendium holds what it should, that a character sheet derives the numbers the book prints, that the rules links resolve and the artwork is being served. It builds a character, checks it, and deletes it. If something is wrong, the failures copy to the clipboard as text.

This system implements the d20 Modern System Reference Document.
